module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures associated with A109908

$a(n)$ = greatest prime of the form $k(n-k)-1$, or $0$ if no such prime exists.

*References:*
- [A109908](https://oeis.org/A109908)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA109908

/--
$a(n)$ = greatest prime of the form $k(n-k)-1$, or $0$ if no such prime exists.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.Icc 1 (n / 2))
  |>.image (fun k => k * (n - k) - 1)
  |>.filter Nat.Prime
  |>.sup id

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 3 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by decide

/--
Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for $n > 3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : ∀ n > 3, a n > 0 := by
  sorry

end OeisA109908

reformulations.difference: The OEIS name says only "greatest prime of the form k*(n-k)-1", with no range for k. The Lean definition restricts k to Finset.Icc 1 (n/2) and computes k*(n-k)-1 with truncated subtraction on ℕ. A reader might worry that k in (n/2, n) is missed, or that junk values from truncated subtraction enter the set.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an integer k ≤ 0 or k ≥ n, k(n-k) ≤ 0, so k(n-k)-1 ≤ -1 is not prime. The expression is symmetric under k ↦ n-k, so every prime of the form comes from some k with 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊n/2⌋, which is also the range the OEIS PARI and Maple programs use. In that range n-k ≥ k ≥ 1, so n-k and k(n-k)-1 are exact on ℕ. Lean proofs in /workspace/review/proof2.lean, using only the standard axioms: `0 < a n ↔ ∃ k : ℤ, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ (p : ℤ) = k * (n - k) - 1`; `a n = 0 ∨ (a n).Prime`; `a n` is at least every prime k(n-k)-1 with 1 ≤ k ≤ n/2. From these, `(∀ n > 3, a n > 0)` is equivalent to the integer-k reading of the OEIS conjecture. `#eval` of `a` agrees with the OEIS b-file for all n = 1..1500.

sources_consulted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A109/A109908.seq (official OEIS data mirror of A109908; oeis.org HTML showed a Cloudflare challenge)
review.notes:
Checks performed:
- `#eval` of `OeisA109908.a` agrees with the OEIS b-file for n = 1..1500. The b-file's only zeros up to n = 10000 are at n = 1, 2, 3.
- `decide +kernel` confirms the conjecture for 4 ≤ n ≤ 30.
- The bound `n > 3` is sharp: `∀ n > 2, a n > 0` is refuted at n = 3.
- `a 0 = 0` lies outside the OEIS offset, and the conjecture never reaches it.
- The tests a_1..a_5 (0, 0, 0, 3, 5) match the OEIS data.

Status: `research open` matches the source. A109908 says "Conjecture: a(n) > 0 for n > 3" and "Conjecture verified up to 10^9 (Fiorentini, Jul 2023)"; its last edit (Oct 2025) records no proof. For even n = 2t the claim says t^2 - 1 is a prime plus a square. That is a special case of Hardy–Littlewood's open Conjecture H, so an open status is plausible.

Unread lead: the sibling A109909 (same existence statement; formalized in FormalConjectures/OEIS/109909.lean) links an unpublished ResearchGate preprint, Pengcheng Niu and Junli Zhang, "On Two Conjectures of A. Murthy" (2024, DOI 10.13140/RG.2.2.16430.11848). I could not read it: ResearchGate returned 403, DataCite has no abstract, and other indexes were rate-limited. Neither OEIS entry records the conjecture as proved, so I report no status issue. A maintainer may want to check what that preprint claims.
